title: Strong formal resolution rules and exact empty-center contraction
statement: For the Noetherian adic formal pairs, ideals, regular maps and blowups of [def-per-rig-regular-formal-pair-geometry], a finite formal blowup tower retains its length, all levels and transitions with identity and composition laws, the initial isomorphism, and every ordered center ideal; each step is its formal blowup and extends the distinguished ideal. A strong resolution has coherent open nonempty regular centers whose images lie in the original input singular locus, and regular terminal level. A contracted formal pullback comparison consists of a monotone count of retained stages at every original level, an ordered embedding of the retained centers, and maps from the repeated contracted levels to the original levels. The level squares are cartesian in adic Noetherian formal schemes with local ideal-preserving maps; the maps commute with all transitions, the retained ideals equal the actual extended ideals, and a stage is omitted if and only if its pulled ideal is the unit ideal at every point. The count starts at zero, ends at the contracted length, increments at every retained stage, and stays constant at every deleted stage. A rig-regular formal resolution rule is one assignment of a finite strong tower to every rig-regular input, compatible in this sense with every regular map of pairs, and assigning length zero to empty inputs. No independence from the distinguished ideal is included.
